template.reload: The selected regular file is read on every GET /; replace it atomically and reload the browser.
template.placeholder_count: Each placeholder must occur exactly once.
template.catalog_source: i18n/*.json remains beside web_backend.py, not in the custom template.

transport.cookie: Open GET / first to receive the process-local qn_ui HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie.

http_errors.400: Malformed request at the HTTP layer
http_errors.403: Missing/expired UI cookie, CSRF or same-origin check
http_errors.409: Public refusal, busy, stale state or unavailable dependency
http_errors.502: Unexpected backend failure with a generic public message

transport.download_exception: note-export returns an attachment with its format-specific MIME; note-media-download returns JSON metadata only.
transport.cache: Cloud reads of notes, summaries, tags, sharing, favorites, quotas and memos are served from a server-side cache for 24 hours, and option lists (translation languages, interpreter options, generation options) for 7 days. A response from the cache carries X-Cached-At (Unix seconds when it was read from the cloud). Send "refresh": true in any POST body to bypass the cache. Writes drop the entries they affect.

GET /api/status.query: Optional ?since=N returns only events with id greater than N. Optional ?settings_revision=R leaves out setting_details and setting_choices when R equals the current settings_revision, which every response carries.
GET /api/status.response: Cached status object: connection, device, settings, generation/notification groups, recording ownership, record_task, device_check, armed, cache (entries, oldest_at), transcript, rtc, live_diagnostics, pending flags, credentials, events, event_cursor, assistant state, settings_revision, action_timings (per action: count, failures, last_ms, max_ms, total_ms since start) and server_time.
GET /api/status.side_effects: None. It reads host memory only and never triggers a vendor refresh.

GET /healthz.query: None. No UI cookie is required, but loopback Host and same-site checks apply.
GET /healthz.side_effects: None. Use before an intentional restart; a safe response does not prove physical device behavior.

account-settings.purpose: Read the account-level settings: smart slicing and voiceprint.
account-settings.response: slicing {enabled} and voiceprint {allowed, enabled, enrolled, available_to_account}.
account-settings.side_effects: Two reads (MoziCustomerSettingAppI.queryCustomerSetting, MoziVoicePrintAppI.getVoicePrintConfig), cached for a day.

assistant.purpose: Send one prompt to the built-in QwenNote assistant or the configured custom provider.

fields.task_uuid: string: listed note UUID, built-in provider only

assistant.response: JSON with text, provider and route or cancellation/provider-outcome metadata.
assistant.side_effects: Starts one bounded provider request. Built-in prompts reuse the backend-held conversation session until assistant-new or assistant-select-conversation. No microphone, device audio, note write or automatic forwarding. Built-in note context requires a listed task_uuid.

assistant-cancel.purpose: Cancel the active host assistant request.
assistant-cancel.response: JSON cancellation state. The provider may already have processed the prompt.
assistant-cancel.side_effects: Cancels local HTTP work only; it cannot retract provider-side processing.

assistant-note-size.purpose: Count the characters of a listed note's saved transcript, shown when the note is attached to a built-in assistant question.

fields.task_uuid: string: note UUID from the owner's notes list

assistant-note-size.response: JSON with characters, paragraphs and complete (false after 2,000 paragraphs). The assistant reports no context use or limit.
assistant-note-size.side_effects: Cloud reads of the transcript pages, served from the server-side cache while fresh.

assistant-conversations.purpose: List saved built-in QwenNote conversations for explicit restoration.
assistant-conversations.response: JSON with conversations[] containing opaque handle, title and date, plus provider and route. Vendor session identifiers are never returned.
assistant-conversations.side_effects: Performs one bounded read-only application request for at most 100 deduplicated conversations and replaces the process-local handle map. No prompt replay, note write, device command or upstream deletion.

assistant-history.purpose: Read the active built-in QwenNote conversation, including prompts and reply completion state.
assistant-history.response: JSON with messages[] containing query, text and complete, plus latest text, provider and route. Session and task identifiers are not returned.
assistant-history.side_effects: Uses the backend-held session ID for one read-only application history request. No prompt replay, note write, device command or upstream deletion.

assistant-new.purpose: Start a fresh built-in conversation on the next prompt.
assistant-new.side_effects: Clears only backend memory for the current session and recovery handle. Existing vendor conversation history is preserved; no upstream request.

assistant-recover.purpose: Recover an interrupted built-in reply by polling its existing vendor task result.
assistant-recover.response: JSON with recovered:true, text, provider and route, or a public error while recovery remains available.
assistant-recover.side_effects: Uses the backend-held task ID for bounded application querySummaryResult polling. Never resends the prompt or creates a note/device operation.

assistant-select-conversation.purpose: Restore one listed built-in conversation and display its current history.
assistant-select-conversation.response: JSON with restored:true, messages[] containing query, text and complete, plus latest text, provider and route. Session and task identifiers are not returned.
assistant-select-conversation.side_effects: Resolves the process-local handle, sets the backend session and performs one read-only history request. Replaces stale local recovery state and exposes recovery only when restored history reports an interrupted task. No prompt replay, note write, device command or upstream deletion.

audio-memos.response: JSON with items containing text, created_at_ms and duration_ms, plus has_more.
audio-memos.side_effects: Read-only application request with a 30-second cache. No media download or device attribution.

ble-pairing-file.purpose: Download the Bluetooth pairing file for tools/a2-ble. Dangerous action.
ble-pairing-file.response: Attachment, not JSON: a2-pairing.json with sn, device_secret, did and corp_id.
ble-pairing-file.side_effects: Reads the A2 serial and device secret from the bound-device record already in memory, and a stable client id kept in .private/ble-client.json. Requires dangerous actions; the values are never shown on the page or logged.

cache-clear.purpose: Delete every saved cloud read, so the next reads go to the cloud.
cache-clear.side_effects: Deletes the cache files in protected storage. Journals, settings and credentials are untouched.

capture-start.purpose: Start bounded private diagnostics on the existing native receive loop.
capture-start.response: Aggregate capture status with elapsed seconds, byte/row counters and limits.
capture-start.side_effects: Writes protected diagnostic data only. Does not start recording, arm controls or call the vendor.

capture-stop.response: Final aggregate capture status; raw capture remains protected.
capture-stop.side_effects: Stops diagnostics only. Never stops a recording.

confirm-stopped.purpose: Manually close the open recording after seeing the A2 stop, when a device check cannot reach the cloud.
confirm-stopped.side_effects: Clears the owned-test journal only after explicit confirmation. This is not a Stop command.

dangerous.purpose: Turn the dangerous-actions switch on or off.

fields.confirm: boolean: must be true to enable

dangerous.side_effects: Saves the switch in .private/dangerous.json; no cloud call.

device-check.purpose: Check the A2 now: online state, battery and, when it reports a current recording, that recording task.
device-check.response: device_check: state (recording, paused, idle, offline, unknown), online, checked_at, battery_percent, in_progress.
device-check.side_effects: One bound-device read and at most one recording-task read. Opens the recording when the A2 is recording (including one started with its button) and closes it when the A2 is idle or offline. Runs automatically every 30 s while a recording is open and every 5 minutes otherwise.

device-identity.purpose: Read the cached public identity projection for the selected bound device.
device-identity.response: JSON with name, sn, firmware_version, read_at, stale, revision, pending and restore availability.
device-identity.side_effects: No native request. Returns owner-only cached name/SN and opaque revision; firmware is null when unavailable.

device-info.purpose: Product information and the phones linked to the A2.
device-info.response: product (productName, deviceType, connectType, bindType, oneDevice) and phones[] (name, state: allowed, blocked or connected).
device-info.side_effects: Two reads (getProductConfig, queryDeviceConnections). The connection request and update calls take the A2 over from the owner's phone and are not offered.

device-name.purpose: Refresh device identity and reconcile any pending rename journal.
device-name.response: Refreshed device-identity object and readback state.
device-name.side_effects: Read-only native reconciliation. Never sends or replays a rename.

device-name-restore.purpose: Restore the journaled original device name.
device-name-restore.response: Device identity with verified readback or pending uncertainty.
device-name-restore.side_effects: One explicit restore write while the requested name is still current. Never automatic.

device-name-save.purpose: Rename the selected bound device through the application path.

fields.name: string: trimmed device name, at most 32 weighted units

device-name-save.response: Device identity with verified readback or pending uncertainty.
device-name-save.side_effects: Single-shot rename with a protected original-name journal and strict readback. Maximum 32 weighted units.

device-unbind.purpose: Unbind the A2 from the account on the server. Dangerous action.
device-unbind.side_effects: One DeviceI.unbindV3 write, journaled first and never retried. The console then loses the device. Binding again needs the official app and Bluetooth (activation reads a cipher from the A2). Requires dangerous actions to be enabled.

disarm.side_effects: Saves the disarmed state. Does not stop an active recording; Stop stays available while a recording is open.

documents.purpose: Invoke one of the 14 read-only QwenNote MCP tools through the host adapter.

fields.tool: string: one of the documented read-only MCP tool names
fields.arguments: object: schema for the selected tool

documents.response: JSON MCP result envelope. The default template decodes its structured content for notes, summaries, transcripts and extras.
documents.side_effects: Read-only MCP call with a 60-second total deadline and no automatic retry. Generic write tools are not exposed.

generation.purpose: Save summary-generation mode, minimum duration and maximum duration as one batch.

fields.values: object: complete auto_generate_minutes, auto_generate_minutes_duration and auto_generate_minutes_duration_limit values
fields.persistent_override: boolean: true only, required for a new persistent override

generation.response: Updated generation-group descriptor and restoration state.
generation.side_effects: Device-setting write requiring readiness and a before-write journal. Persistent inherited overrides require confirmation.

mcp-login-finish.purpose: Finish an MCP login with the address the browser ended on, when it could not return to the console by itself.

fields.url: string: the full address from the browser bar after approving

mcp-login-finish.side_effects: Exchanges the one-time code (PKCE) at the token endpoint and stores the tokens in the reader's format: the read store for read access, .private/write for write access. GET /mcp/callback does the same when the vendor returns to the console.

mcp-login-start.purpose: Start owner consent for MCP read or write access, returning to this console's own port.

fields.return_to: string: console (default; the vendor returns to /mcp/callback on this port) or registered (the address the existing client was registered with; then paste the final address)

mcp-login-start.response: url to open in a new tab, and return_to.
mcp-login-start.side_effects: Reads the public authorization-server metadata and keeps a one-time PKCE login in backend memory for 15 minutes. Reuses the existing client registration; registers nothing.

memo-delete.purpose: Delete a voice memo. Dangerous action.
memo-delete.side_effects: One deleteMission; requires dangerous actions; journaled, never retried.

memo-update.side_effects: One DingerAiAssistantI.updateMission (content), as the app edits memos; journaled, never retried.

note-delete.purpose: Delete a note permanently. Dangerous action; notes have no recycle bin.
note-delete.side_effects: One PortalMinutesI.deleteTaskV2 write after a fresh identity read, journaled first and never retried. Requires dangerous actions to be enabled.

note-export.purpose: Download an original, translated or bilingual note transcript or default summary in an application-supported format.

fields.target_language: string: language key returned by note-translate-options; omit for the original
fields.bilingual: boolean: include source text with the translation; requires target_language, default false
fields.file_format: string: txt, markdown, docx or pdf; transcript also allows srt; default txt

note-export.response: Attachment, not JSON: text/plain, text/markdown, DOCX or PDF. Request with download handling and create a Blob.
note-export.side_effects: Target/format validation, application export and bounded host download with text decoding or DOCX/PDF signature checks. Vendor Markdown transport may be text/plain or text/markdown; binary responses may omit Content-Disposition, but the host response always uses attachment. No note edit or saved-language change; 8 MiB response limit and no automatic retry.

note-favorite.purpose: Favorite or unfavorite a listed note.

fields.expected_collected: boolean: state shown before the click

note-favorite.response: JSON with collected, cloud acknowledgement, readback and verification state.
note-favorite.side_effects: One application-path collectMinutes write after a fresh expected-state check and protected journal.

note-favorite-status.purpose: Read favorite state and reconcile a matching pending journal.
note-favorite-status.response: JSON with collected, verified true and changed false.
note-favorite-status.side_effects: Native read only. Cannot clear a journal belonging to another note.

note-markers.purpose: List a note's markers, or add a marker at a time.

fields.add_ms: integer: milliseconds from the start; adds a marker first

note-markers.response: markers[] with kind (marker, image, text), time_ms and text.
note-markers.side_effects: MinutesNoteI.queryNoteList; with add_ms, one createNote (type 0) first, journaled, never retried.

note-mcp-write.purpose: Change a note or the personal hot words through an MCP write tool, as an alternative to the native application path.

fields.tool: string: update_minutes_title, update_minutes_summary, replace_minutes_text, replace_speaker, add_personal_hot_word or delete_personal_hotword
fields.arguments: object: taskUuid (listed note) plus title, summaryText, originalText and replacedText, or speakerNick and targetNickName; hotWordList (1 to 50 words) for the hot-word tools

note-mcp-write.response: tool, applied true and the MCP result envelope.
note-mcp-write.side_effects: One MCP tools/call on the separate owner-consented write grant (artifacts/mcp-reader/.private/write, scope qwennote:read qwennote:write). The intent is journaled first; an unknown outcome is never retried. Drops the note's saved cloud reads. Available only when status.mcp_write_available is true and the server advertises the tool to that grant.

note-media-download.purpose: Save a cloud-stored original audio recording into protected host storage.
note-media-download.response: JSON with saved, random local filename, byte count, SHA-256, MIME, source, expected duration and ffprobe audio metadata. Signed URLs and absolute host paths are excluded.
note-media-download.side_effects: Reads minutesDetailV2, queryPlayInfo and queryDownloadUrl, then downloads once to .private/media with mode 0700 and file mode 0600. A rejected or empty download-URL reply falls back to the official mobile/PC play URL; detail/play failures and missing URLs refuse the save. Requires audio mediaType audio, application non-incognito semantics (isIncognitoMode other than true), current cloud storage 0 and current incognito mode 0. HTTPS origin allowlist, public-DNS pinning, redirects disabled, 512 MiB cap, 300-second transfer bound, ffprobe audio validation and partial-file cleanup. Writes protected note-media.json without URLs or paths; no setting or note writes and no automatic retry.

note-regenerate.purpose: Regenerate the default Markdown summary through the two-stage application flow.
note-regenerate.response: JSON with accepted/pending state and, when complete, summary text and revision.
note-regenerate.side_effects: Starts manualRegenerateSummary then generateMinutesSummary. Completion is asynchronous; refresh reconciles without replay.

fields.replace: string: literal replacement, may be empty

note-replace-preview.response: JSON with matches, changed paragraph count, before/after rows and an opaque revision.
note-replace-preview.side_effects: Read-only full native transcript snapshot. Invalidated when find or replace input changes.

note-replace-save.purpose: Apply a fresh transcript replacement preview.
note-replace-save.response: JSON with verified readback or pending uncertainty.
note-replace-save.side_effects: One bounded updateParagraph batch, at most 20 changed paragraphs and 1000 matches. Marked paragraphs are refused.

note-share.purpose: Read private/public note-sharing state and preserved options.
note-share.response: JSON with access, enabled options, sharing flag, revision and pending state. Passwords, role codes and subresource IDs are not exposed.
note-share.side_effects: Native application read only; also reconciles exact original/requested journal states without a write.

note-share-save.purpose: Set note scope to private or public.

fields.password: string: 4 to 16 letters and digits with public access; empty string removes the password

note-share-save.response: Updated sharing state with strict readback or pending uncertainty.
note-share-save.side_effects: Explicit scope write with protected journal. Public mutation is prohibited by the current project constraint.

note-share-url.purpose: Read the application-provided HTTPS share URL for explicit clipboard copying in the current private or public scope.
note-share-url.response: JSON with url, access and sharing_enabled. The URL is sensitive and is returned only to this explicit request.
note-share-url.side_effects: Two native application reads. No scope write, URL opening, external transmission or journal mutation.

note-speaker-rename.purpose: Rename a speaker across a note through the application path.

fields.from: string: current speaker name, as shown
fields.to: string: new speaker name, at most 64 characters

note-speaker-rename.side_effects: Reads the whole transcript, picks the paragraphs of that speaker (as the app's 'all' choice does) and sends one batchUpdateParagraphNickName; journaled, never retried.

note-summary.purpose: Read the complete default Markdown summary.
note-summary.response: JSON with text, revision, verified and pending.
note-summary.side_effects: Native read and read-only journal reconciliation for a recently listed own note.

note-summary-save.response: Updated summary text/revision with verified readback or pending uncertainty.
note-summary-save.side_effects: One editFullTextSummary write with fresh revision check and original journal. Maximum 48 KiB.

note-tag-create.purpose: Create an account tag with automatic matching off.

fields.name: string: trimmed, at most 15 UTF-16 units

note-tag-create.response: Updated tag options and revision. The new tag is not assigned automatically.
note-tag-create.side_effects: One addTag write with fresh catalog, protected journal, acknowledged-ID readback and no automatic retry.

note-tag-delete.purpose: Delete a tag definition that is not assigned to the open note.
note-tag-delete.side_effects: One deleteTag write after fresh membership checks. Existing assignments must be preserved.

note-tag-rename.purpose: Rename a tag and optionally change its automatic-matching flag.

fields.name: string: trimmed, at most 15 UTF-16 units

note-tag-rename.side_effects: One updateTag write. Hidden description is preserved; omitted auto_match preserves the current flag.

note-tags.purpose: Read account tag options and memberships for the open note.
note-tags.response: JSON with options, selected_handles, revision, verified and pending.
note-tags.side_effects: Native catalog and membership reads. Opaque handles keep raw tag IDs in the backend.

note-tags-save.purpose: Replace the complete set of tags assigned to the open note.

fields.selected_handles: array of strings: complete desired opaque-handle set

note-tags-save.response: Updated selected_handles, options and revision with readback state.
note-tags-save.side_effects: One complete membership replacement with original journal. Does not edit tag definitions.

fields.next_token: string or null: null starts a fresh page; otherwise use the issued token

note-transcript.response: JSON with rows containing text/speaker/timing, next_token and note identity.
note-transcript.side_effects: Read-only application paging, 200 rows per page. Continuation tokens expire after 15 minutes and reject stale notes.

note-translate.purpose: Read a translated title, default summary, brief sections and one transcript page.

fields.target_language: string: target key from note-translate-options; use for a new view
fields.next_token: string: issued continuation token; use instead of target_language

note-translate.response: JSON with title, summary, brief_items, rows and next_token.
note-translate.side_effects: Separate translated view only. Never changes the original note or saved language preference.

note-translate-options.purpose: List supported translation targets and detect the note source language.
note-translate-options.response: JSON with source_language and targets containing key/label.
note-translate-options.side_effects: Native language-catalog read only. No preference write.

notes-browse.purpose: Search all notes, list favorites or a tag, or list the tags to filter by.

fields.mode: string: search, favorites, tag or tags
fields.tag: string: tag handle from mode tags (tag)

notes-browse.response: items[] in the notes-list shape (uuid, title, gmtCreate, durationMillis, collected), or tags[] with handle and name.
notes-browse.side_effects: One read (searchA1Minutes, queryCollectedMinutes, fetchMinutesListByTag or getHomeTabList). Listed notes become usable for note actions.

notification.purpose: Save task-completion alert method and optionally its organization.

fields.method: string: 0 for voice or 1 for vibration
fields.organization_handle: string: opaque option handle; omit to preserve current organization
fields.persistent_override: boolean: true only when confirming an inherited override

notification.response: Updated notification-group descriptor and restoration state.
notification.side_effects: Device-setting write requiring readiness. Organization handles are revalidated; unchanged values cause no write.

notification-options.purpose: Load alert and organization option descriptors.
notification-options.response: Notification-group object with method choices, organization options and opaque handles.
notification-options.side_effects: Read-only listActiveOrganizations request. No physical readiness required.

quotas.purpose: Read membership and remaining account/device quotas, allowance detail and 4G usage.

fields.organization_handle: string: current opaque organization option; omit for the default personal scope

quotas.response: JSON with queried_at, selected opaque organization handle/label and account, device, detail, traffic sections. Each section has available and data.
quotas.side_effects: Four read-only native application requests for the selected scope, with per-section availability, caching and no device mutation. Raw organization IDs stay backend-only.

ready.purpose: Arm the recording and RTC controls until Disarm.
ready.response: armed true, ready_until (far future) and server_time.
ready.side_effects: Saves the armed state in protected storage, so it survives restarts. Sends no device command. The earlier body with physical_ready, device_idle and disposable_only all true is still accepted.

reconnect.purpose: Restart a stopped native connection worker.
reconnect.side_effects: Creates no second refresh owner. Refused while the existing worker runs.

record.purpose: Send a Record, Pause, Resume or Stop command to the A2.

fields.action: string: start, pause, resume or stop

record.response: JSON command acknowledgement and physical_result unverified; the device check about 8 s later shows the result.
record.side_effects: Start first runs a device check and is refused when the A2 is offline or already recording. Pause, resume and stop need an open recording (started here or found by a device check). Ambiguous commands are never retried.

record-task.purpose: Refresh the last observed account/device-matched cloud recording task.
record-task.response: Public record_task summary with cloud status, timestamps, real_time_asr and physical_state_verified false.
record-task.side_effects: Explicit native read. Does not accept IDs, change ownership or mutate the device.

recording-audio.purpose: Save one recording's original audio in protected storage and download it.
recording-audio.response: Attachment, not JSON: the audio file.
recording-audio.side_effects: DeviceFileI.queryFileDownloadInfo, then a bounded, origin-checked download with the cloud-supplied headers into .private/media (0600), checked with ffprobe. Works for incognito recordings too.

recording-delete.purpose: Move a recording to the recycle bin, or delete it permanently. Dangerous action.

fields.permanent: boolean: true deletes permanently; default false moves to the recycle bin
fields.confirm: string: delete, required when permanent is true

recording-delete.side_effects: One DeviceFileI.deleteFiles write (state 3 recycle bin, state 1 permanent), journaled first and never retried. Requires dangerous actions to be enabled.

recording-group-delete.purpose: Delete a recording group. Dangerous action.
recording-group-delete.side_effects: One deleteFileGroups; what happens to the group's recordings is not shown by the app. Requires dangerous actions.

recording-group-save.purpose: Create a recording group, or rename one.
recording-group-save.side_effects: One createFileGroup or updateFileGroup (a full replace with the other fields unchanged); journaled, never retried.

recording-groups.purpose: List the recording groups with file counts.
recording-groups.response: groups[] with handle, name and files; counts (total, ungrouped, recycle_bin).

recording-make-note.purpose: Ask the cloud to turn a recording into a note.
recording-make-note.side_effects: One DeviceTaskI.createGenerateMinutesTask write, journaled first and never retried. The note appears in the list when the cloud finishes.

recording-marker-delete.purpose: Delete a recording marker or text note.

recording-marker-save.purpose: Add a marker or text note to a recording, or edit a text note.

fields.time_ms: integer: milliseconds from the start (to add)
fields.text: string: note text, at most 2000 characters; without it a plain marker is added
fields.marker: string: marker handle (to edit its text)

recording-marker-save.side_effects: One DeviceNoteI.createNote (noteType 0 or 2) or updateNote; journaled, never retried.

recording-markers.purpose: List the markers and text notes of a recording.
recording-markers.response: markers[] with handle, kind, time_ms and text.
recording-markers.side_effects: One DeviceNoteI.queryNoteList read by the recording's fid.

recording-move.purpose: Move a recording into a group.

fields.group: string: group handle from a recording or the group list

recording-recover.purpose: Restore a recording from the recycle bin.
recording-recover.side_effects: One DeviceFileI.recoverFiles write, journaled first and never retried.

recordings.purpose: List the A2's recordings stored in the cloud, including ones that are not notes yet.

fields.next_token: string: issued continuation token for the next page

recordings.response: recordings[] with handle, name, duration_ms, bytes, created_at_ms, note_state (not-transcribed, transcribing, transcribed, failed), incognito, in_recycle_bin, playable_from_cloud; has_more and next_token.
recordings.side_effects: One DeviceFileI.queryFileList read. File ids stay in the backend; the page gets opaque handles.

refresh.purpose: Refresh native discovery, reported settings and generation configuration.
refresh.side_effects: Read-only native refresh. Does not arm controls or change settings.

restore.purpose: Restore an existing individual device-setting override from its journal.
restore.response: Updated setting descriptor and restoration state.
restore.side_effects: One restoration write. Cannot claim to restore unsupported inheritance.

restore-generation.purpose: Restore the complete original summary-generation group.
restore-generation.side_effects: Restores only an exactly restorable device-scope journal; no partial inheritance claim.

restore-notification.purpose: Restore the original notification method and organization.
restore-notification.side_effects: Restores only an exactly restorable journal; the old organization must remain available.

rtc-options.purpose: Read realtime language and voice options for a scene.
rtc-options.response: JSON with languages and nested voices, each using labels and opaque handles.
rtc-options.side_effects: Read-only native configuration with a five-minute cache. No conference or subscription is created.

rtc-start.purpose: Start a realtime transcription session: the recorder Live transcript mode (until Stop, up to 4 hours) or a short Dev test.

fields.seconds: integer: 1 to 14400, default 20; capped just before the session renewal

rtc-start.response: Accepted RTC state; later status carries completion and aggregate receive counters.
rtc-start.side_effects: Creates an experimental recording/conference after ownership checks. Optional audio is receive-only, not played or saved.

rtc-stop.purpose: Stop the owned RTC task and complete conference cleanup.
rtc-stop.side_effects: Cancels the owned task and performs stop/close/readback even after readiness expiry.

setting.purpose: Change one supported individual device setting.

fields.value: string: one of the current setting choices
fields.persistent_override: boolean: true only when confirming a new persistent override

setting.response: Updated setting descriptor and restoration state.
setting.side_effects: Requires readiness, idle test state, scope/choice validation and a before-write journal.

slicing-save.purpose: Turn smart slicing of long recordings on or off for the account.
slicing-save.response: The account settings after a fresh read.
slicing-save.side_effects: One updateCustomerSetting write (smart_slice / enable_slice), journaled first and never retried. Requires armed controls.

voiceprint-clear.purpose: Delete the enrolled voiceprint. Dangerous action.
voiceprint-clear.response: The account settings after a fresh read.
voiceprint-clear.side_effects: One clearVoicePrint write, journaled first and never retried. Requires armed controls and dangerous actions.

voiceprint-save.purpose: Turn voiceprint speaker recognition on or off.
voiceprint-save.response: The account settings after a fresh read.
voiceprint-save.side_effects: One toggleVoicePrint write with shouldClearVoicePrint false, journaled first and never retried. Requires armed controls. Enrolling a voiceprint needs the official app and Bluetooth.
